question: Does the V15 Hebrew↔glyph operator-fingerprint correspondence survive removal of boundary position, long-segment effects, proper-name operators, and loose frequency matching?
claimBoundary: A pass supports transferable cross-corpus similarity of internal local transition fingerprints after explicit boundary, segment-length, proper-name, and frequency controls. It does not establish translation, semantic identity, historical contact, common authorship, theological identity, phonetic equivalence, causal mechanism, or machine execution.

hebrewSource.tokenIdentity: first numeric lemma component rendered H<number>
hebrewSource.properNameControl: OSHB morphology is used only to mark/exclude Hebrew operator identities with any proper-noun-tagged train occurrence; morphology never enters a fingerprint or a pairing score

projector.eligibleCurrentPositions: only positions with four real predecessors and a real successor; no START padding and no END outcome
projector.incomingState: first-occurrence canonical equality pattern of exactly the previous four operator identities; current operator identity is excluded
projector.outcomePrecedence: SAME_CURRENT, then nearest H1..H4, otherwise OTHER; no whole-segment seen/new distinction
projector.segmentContributionControl: segments outside length 6..10 are excluded and each accepted segment contributes at most three deterministically hash-selected internal events

training.pairSelection: mutual nearest neighbor by weighted cosine similarity among train-only candidates whose within-corpus operator-frequency percentiles differ by at most 0.15

evaluation.primaryMetric: mean weighted cosine similarity of evaluable frozen train-paired operators
evaluation.rankMetric: median percentile rank of each frozen glyph among evaluable frozen glyphs
evaluation.fullAdjudication: both holdout and control must independently pass every lane gate plus evaluability gates; these lanes were previously opened, so a pass is a frozen mechanistic stress-test result rather than fresh independent confirmation
